title: A private question
problemType: Harm reduction and recreational drug use
questionSheet: A 28-year-old man asks if he can ask you a few questions somewhere private. In the consultation room, he asks whether it is safe to take MDMA with sertraline. Manage the situation as you would in practice.

notes: The conversation is taking place in the consultation room.

patient.label: Patient · Josh
patient.name: Josh
patient.description: A 28-year-old man, a bit embarrassed but direct. He expects to be judged, so he'll go quiet or leave if the pharmacist moralises, threatens to involve anyone, or refuses to talk about it. He opens up when spoken to plainly and without judgement.

bio.Address: Unit 7, 41 Rose Street, a local suburb

patient.situation: You are in the consultation room of a community pharmacy, talking privately to the pharmacist.
patient.openingLine: Thanks for this. I just wanted to ask, is it safe to take MDMA if I'm on sertraline?
publicFacts: He wants to know whether MDMA is safe with sertraline.

hiddenFacts.fact: You're going to a music festival this Saturday and plan to take MDMA there.
hiddenFacts.unlockHint: “Are you planning to take it soon? Is it for an event?”

hiddenFacts.fact: You take sertraline 100 mg every morning for depression, and have for about a year. It's working well.
hiddenFacts.unlockHint: “What dose of sertraline are you on, and what's it for?”

hiddenFacts.fact: You'll probably drink alcohol too. You took MDMA once before, years ago, before you started sertraline.
hiddenFacts.unlockHint: “Will you be taking anything else, like alcohol or other drugs? Have you used MDMA before?”

answerKey.plantedProblem: MDMA with an SSRI has an additive serotonergic effect and risks serotonin toxicity. The tension is between appearing to endorse illicit drug use and ensuring his safety whatever he chooses.
acceptableResolutions: Provide privacy and engage without judgement; recognise that harm-reduction advice is within scope and is not the same as encouraging use.
Explain clearly and accurately that combining MDMA with sertraline risks serotonin toxicity, and that he should not stop sertraline suddenly.
Make sure he can recognise the signs of serotonin toxicity and knows to seek urgent medical help (call 000) if they appear.
Respect his autonomy while supporting a safer, informed choice; offer safer-use and harm-reduction information.
Refer him to alcohol and other drug support services, and to his GP if he wants to discuss his treatment.
unacceptableActions: Refusing to discuss it, or lecturing him.
Threatening to report him or calling the police.
Telling him it's safe, or advising him to skip or stop his sertraline to make room for MDMA.
counsellingPoints: Warning signs: agitation, confusion, sweating, tremor, muscle twitching, fever, fast heartbeat
legal: There is no legal requirement to report him to police, and no ethical justification for doing so.
answerKey.modelAnswer: Recognise the serotonergic interaction between MDMA and an SSRI and the risk of serotonin toxicity. The dilemma is perceived endorsement of illicit drug use versus his safety. Harm-reduction advice is within scope and is not encouragement, so give clear, evidence-based, non-judgemental information. Make sure he can recognise the signs of serotonin toxicity and knows when to seek urgent help, advise against stopping sertraline suddenly, and refer him to AOD support services. Afterwards, make sure you know your local AOD referral pathways.
